words.gram: particle in the set phrase да ну
dative singular, masculine; with плохо = feels unwell
predicative, + dative of the person + infinitive

examples.trans: Very well! Have a pleasant evening.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask (for), to request', paired with 'просить'.

examples.trans: I wanted to ask you something.
Arkash, I wanted to ask you something.

meanings.note: Core Russian name meaning 'California' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Will you ask for a California roll?

examples.text: Это слово «калифорния» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'California' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: short for скорая помощь; declines like an adjective

examples.text: Тут кнопки вызова: скорая, полиция и мы.
examples.trans: Here are the call buttons: ambulance, police, and us.

meanings.en: to call for, to summon (a taxi, driver, police, doctor)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to summon', paired with 'вызывать'.

examples.text: Ты же не помнишь ничего. Ты вызвал трезвого водителя!
examples.trans: You don't remember anything, after all. You called a sober driver!

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.
